answered.sql: SELECT Salary FROM MedicalRoles WHERE RoleID IN (SELECT RoleID FROM Hospitals_Medical_Roles GROUP BY RoleID HAVING COUNT(HospitalID) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Hospitals))

candidates.meaning: Find the salary of the role that each hospital has, implying each hospital has at least one role and we should list the role's salary for each hospital.
candidates.sql: SELECT H.Name AS HospitalName, MR.RoleName, MR.Salary FROM Hospitals H JOIN Hospitals_Medical_Roles HMR ON H.HospitalID = HMR.HospitalID JOIN MedicalRoles MR ON HMR.RoleID = MR.RoleID

candidates.meaning: Find the salary of the most common role at each hospital.
candidates.sql: SELECT H.Name, MR.RoleName, MR.Salary FROM Hospitals H JOIN Hospitals_Medical_Roles HM ON H.HospitalID = HM.HospitalID JOIN MedicalRoles MR ON HM.RoleID = MR.RoleID GROUP BY H.Name, MR.RoleName ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

candidates.meaning: Find the salary of any role that each hospital has, without considering the frequency of roles.
candidates.sql: SELECT H.Name, MR.RoleName, MR.Salary FROM Hospitals H JOIN Hospitals_Medical_Roles HM ON H.HospitalID = HM.HospitalID JOIN MedicalRoles MR ON HM.RoleID = MR.RoleID

candidates.meaning: Find the salary of the role that each hospital has, assuming each hospital has only one role.
candidates.sql: SELECT H.Name, MR.RoleName, MR.Salary FROM Hospitals H JOIN Hospitals_Medical_Roles HM ON H.HospitalID = HM.HospitalID JOIN MedicalRoles MR ON HM.RoleID = MR.RoleID LIMIT 1
